keyVerseText: O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun אֹמֶן (ʼômen) derives from the root אָמַן (ʼâman), which conveys the idea of establishing, supporting, and fostering. This root suggests a sense of firmness and reliability, akin to building up or nurturing something to stability and trustworthiness. Unlike the general English term 'truth,' the root meaning emphasizes a foundational, steadfast faithfulness that undergirds trust and assurance.
usageInScripture: The word אֹמֶן appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, highlighting its specific and weighty significance. It is translated as 'truth' or 'faithfulness,' indicating a consistent theme of reliability and steadfastness in divine counsel. This singular occurrence, paired with its translation as 'and truth,' underscores the inseparability of faithfulness and truth in the biblical understanding of God's nature and actions.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֹמֶן as rooted in firm establishment and nurturing faithfulness deepens our appreciation for God's character as unchanging and trustworthy. This word reveals that God's promises and counsels are not merely true in abstract terms but are firmly grounded in His faithful nature. For the Christian faith, this assures believers that God's word and covenant are secure and dependable, inviting a response of trust and praise. It also points to the faithfulness of Christ, who embodies and fulfills God's steadfastness toward His people.
keyVerseReflection: Isaiah 25:1 declares, 'O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth.' Here, אֹמֶן contributes the profound sense that God's ancient plans are not only true but firmly established and trustworthy. This assures believers that God's purposes are reliable and enduring, worthy of exaltation and praise. It highlights the inseparable bond between God's faithfulness and truth as the foundation of our confidence in Him.
